Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Baltimore MD/Washington DC
910 PM EDT Mon Jul 20 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
Made a few changes to the gridded database to try to hone in on
timing for Tuesday's severe weather threat, but the overall
message remains the same. 

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
- Strong to severe thunderstorms are likely Tuesday, with
  some thunderstorm risk lingering into Wednesday.

- Cooler than average temperatures anticipated beginning
  Thursday through the end of the week.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
KEY MESSAGE 1...Strong to severe thunderstorms are likely Tuesday, with
 some thunderstorm risk lingering into Wednesday.

Moisture is expected to return in earnest tonight in 
strengthening srly flow. Elevated showers and thunderstorms are 
possible overnight into Tue morning as a front returns 
northward. Morning low clouds and a cap will likely delay 
convective initiation until the mid afternoon, but afternoon 
temps in the low 90s combined with at least low 70s dewpoints 
should result in strong instability with 1500-2000 J/kg CAPE 
progged. This combined with approaching anomalous upper level 
trough and associated strong wind speeds aloft, particularly for
the peak of summer should provide ample forcing and shear to 
result in a significant severe wx episode Tue. Scattered 
significant wind damage reports seem likely, with the potential 
for isolated tornadoes, and perhaps flash flooding. Flash flood 
threat does not appear significant enough for a watch given 
anticipated fast storm motions of 30kt or more.

By Wednesday, there is some uncertainty with the cold frontal 
position. With the upper trough overhead, additional showers 
and thunderstorms are likely, especially across southern
Maryland. While some additional strong to severe thunderstorms 
can't be ruled out if things trend slower, it's beginning to 
appear the best parameters for that to occur will be shunted 
toward southeast Virginia.


KEY MESSAGE 2...Cooler than average temperatures anticipated 
beginning Thursday through the end of the week.

An upper-level trough centered over southeastern Canada will 
track towards the northeast on Thursday, allowing high pressure 
to slide into the region from the west. This resulting high 
pressure could persist through early Sunday. Dewpoints will also
trend lower during this period, resulting in relatively dry 
conditions. Temperatures range in the low-to-mid 80s, trending 
slightly below average for July. This high pressure could begin 
to break down late this weekend as a strong upper-level trough 
begins to form over the Great Lakes region. As the trailing cold
front transitions east, humidity and precipitation chances 
could begin to increase again at the start of next week as this 
system moves through.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z TUESDAY THROUGH SATURDAY/...
A few showers and storms are already popping up in central VA
towards CHO. These may increase in coverage through the 
overnight hours, and perhaps even reach the other terminals by 
just before daybreak. MRB has the lowest chance, with the metro 
terminals probably sitting around a 40% chance, but included 
PROB30s for all for now. 

Multiple rounds of thunderstorms are likely after this initial 
activity, one between 19Z-21Z, and the other one coming later in
the evening. Storms could linger well into the overnight. 
Especially with the afternoon storms, damaging wind gusts are 
possible, along with the potential for some large hail. 
 
More storms are possible Wed, particularly eastern terminals. 
Severe wind gusts of 50-kt or greater are the main threat. 

Prevailing VFR conditions are likely across terminals Friday and 
Saturday. Light northeast winds begin to shift southerly late 
Saturday night.

&&

.MARINE...
Strengthening srly flow tonight is expected to result in SCA
conditions. Gusty SSW winds expected Tue through Tue night with
likelihood of strong gusts over 33 kt, which will likely require
SMWs. SCAs have been extended through Tue night into Wed
morning.

Winds stay below SCA thresholds Friday and through the weekend. 5-10 
knot winds flow northeast before shifting southerly late Saturday 
night.

&&

.TIDES/COASTAL FLOODING...
Increasing SE to S flow from this evening into Tuesday will 
lead to water levels reaching Action stages.

&&
